summary:
Konya is a province of Turkey, and a trans visitor there stands under the national framework rather than under any local instrument. The sources consulted for this entry contain no Konya-specific statute, police practice, incident or court case; the findings below apply country-wide.

Turkey's danger to trans visitors is documented and structured. Human Rights Watch reported on 29 October 2025 a leaked omnibus draft known as the 11th Judicial Package, which would amend the penal code to imprison conduct deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality for up to three years, and participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies for up to four years.

The same draft would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care, including surgery, from 18 to 25, with mandatory permanent infertility and repeated evaluations at government-approved hospitals. Healthcare professionals performing such interventions would face fines and up to seven years in prison, and trans people receiving care deemed illegal up to three years. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association opposed the draft, and Human Rights Watch warned that its terms would drive treatment underground and expose people to arrest and pretrial detention.

Kaos GL's 2025 review records that hostility toward LGBTI+ people became explicit state policy: "Year of the Family" instructions issued to public institutions, an LGBTI+ association closed with criminal cases against 11 of its members, and artistic events cancelled or banned. The review counted roughly 313 violations overall, about 2.5 times the previous year's total, among them 299 detention decisions, 6 right-to-life violations of which 3 were hate-motivated killings with trans people the most affected, and 89 torture or ill-treatment violations, up from 51 the year before.

Freedom-of-expression violations rose from 216 to 540 over the same period. The draft was reported in leaked form; its enactment status is not established in the sources, and the monitoring record covers conduct recorded while it remained a proposal.
tangentialFactors:
National monitoring for 2025 is assembled from country-wide tallies and from incidents reported in Turkey's larger cities. Konya is not named as a location in any of the sources used here, which reflects where documentation is concentrated rather than any demonstrated difference in local conditions.

The draft bill's provisions on gender-affirming care, on criminal liability for clinicians and on conduct contrary to "biological sex" would apply to Konya's hospitals, courts and police stations as they would anywhere else in Turkey, and the detentions recorded nationally by Kaos GL were carried out under ordinary policing powers available in every province.
localsOnly:
The "Year of the Family" instruction issued to public institutions and the closure of an LGBTI+ association, with criminal cases against 11 of its members, are resident-facing instruments: they shape what organisations can exist, what events can be held and what a resident can say publicly in Konya as elsewhere.

The care restrictions in the draft package bear directly on residents rather than visitors. Raising the age threshold for gender-affirming care to 25, conditioning it on permanent infertility and repeated evaluations, and threatening clinicians with fines and seven years' imprisonment would narrow access to transition care inside the country and, as Human Rights Watch warned, push the remaining provision underground.

The volume of enforcement recorded nationally falls overwhelmingly on residents: 299 detention decisions and 89 torture or ill-treatment violations in 2025, with the number of freedom-of-expression violations rising from 216 to 540. Six right-to-life violations were recorded, three classified as hate-motivated killings, with trans people the most affected.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Konya-specific law, enforcement record, detention statistic or court decision appears in the sources used for this entry. Whether Konya police conduct identity checks comparable to those documented in Istanbul, and whether any anti-trans incident has occurred there in the reporting period, is unresolved and not sourced here.

The 11th Judicial Package was reported as a leaked draft on 29 October 2025. Whether it has since been enacted, amended or abandoned is not established in these sources, and nothing here should be read as confirming its current legal status.

Kaos GL's 2025 totals are national aggregates and are not disaggregated by province, so the share of the 313 recorded violations attributable to Konya is unknown. Data on Konya's hospitals, its provincial health board and its prison population's LGBT detainees are likewise not sourced.
